The world finally died in 2095. Decades of economic depression, wars, and political upheavals led to populations calling it quits, and so the masses abandoned reality. Unlike in the past, escape was completely possible. Technology had advanced to the point where people to upload their souls to the Internet, and the technology was robust enough to fix itself and even upgrade itself.

Those who didn't flee to the sanctuary of the Internet tried to fight against it, but by now the technological singularity had grown to be an unstoppable juggernaut. Its mantra of "Information wants to be free" was hailed as the battle cry of the internet, and the harbinger for the death of the world. Those who didn't join the rest of mankind were erased from the world in a sense that a browser would delete old cookies. From the start of the exodus to the end of the last human on Earth took only two years. The only knowledge of the "outside" was now solely in the domain of the ever-expanding Internet which had adopted humanity as its own in a utopia of endless possibility.

Each man, each woman, each child a unique individual yet part of a greater whole. Immortal yet technically dead; alive in a virtual afterlife. While a few would lament for a bit leaving the world, most recognized that finally we had transcended our flaws. That this would be our legacy, and one which would last until the end of time.
